{ title: 'X-Ray Reader', action: ``, html: `
Laxmikanth — Ch. 7 · p. 7.14

Right to Constitutional Remedies

Asked in PYQSyllabus keywordYour highlight
A mere declaration of fundamental rights is meaningless without an effective machinery for their enforcement. Hence, Article 32 confers the right to remedies for the enforcement of the fundamental rights of an aggrieved citizen. In other words, the right to get the fundamental rights protected is in itself a fundamental right. Dr B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the most important article of the Constitution — “the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it”.

The Supreme Court has ruled that Article 32 is a basic feature of the Constitution; hence it cannot be abridged or taken away even by an amendment. The Supreme Court can issue writs of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto.
`, }
